column11: Why does mild-moderate ATN produce a rising MAG3 nephrogram despite relatively preserved blood flow?
column12: MAG3 reaches the kidney through renal perfusion and is cleared predominantly by proximal tubular extraction and secretion. In mild-moderate ATN, perfusion may remain relatively normal, so tracer delivery is preserved, but tubular handling and excretion are impaired. Cortical activity therefore accumulates or remains retained instead of falling, producing a rising nephrogram with reduced excretion. With more severe injury or cortical necrosis, flow and cortical uptake also decline.

⚠️ Pearls / Pitfalls
  • Technical mimics of ARF include poor bolus, dose extravasation, and radiopharmaceutical impurity.
  • Urine leak can mimic ARF through increased BUN/creatinine from reabsorbed recycled creatinine and decreased urine output; progressive extra-urinary tracer confirms leak.
  • Marked hydronephrosis without obstruction may clear poorly even after diuretic; postural drainage can help.
  • A distended bladder on postvoid images suggests bladder outlet obstruction or neurogenic bladder; repeat with bladder catheter to confirm impact on kidneys.
  • An ectopic or ptotic kidney can mimic unilateral renal failure if imaged only posteriorly.

📊 Clinical / Prognostic Pivots
  • Community-acquired ARF accounts for about 1% of hospital admissions; up to 20% of critical-care admissions develop hospital-acquired ARF.
  • Mortality may be as high as 50-70% overall, while prerenal etiologies are most often reversible with approximately 7% mortality.

⭐ Super Summary
  • Read the renogram as delivery, cortical handling, then drainage: low delivery suggests prerenal/vascular disease; preserved flow with cortical retention favors ATN; persistent collecting-system activity suggests obstruction; progressive tracer outside the urinary tract indicates urine leak.
